incident-bot: ALERT: Increased OOMs detected on prod-gpu cluster (rvw-prod-gpu-05, rvw-prod-gpu-12). 12 OOMs in last 10m, node restarts detected, paging lag rising. Link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/oom-spike :rotating_light:
Maria C.: I'm on it — seeing gradual resident growth on the KV paged allocator for a handful of long-lived containers. Not a sudden spike, more like slow creep over ~36-48h.
Alex R.: which processes? any obvious leak stack?
Maria C.: mostly inference-worker processes serving llama-13b-like variants. kvcache resident size on rvw-prod-gpu-05: 42GB -> 61GB over 48h. attention_paged allocator fragmentation metric shows >75% fragmented pages.
Maria C.: logs from the container just before restart:
```
[2026-03-15 02:12:44] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15 02:12:44] runtime: OOM killer invoked, container exit code 137
[2026-03-15 02:12:45] sweeper: started pass, scanned 128k pages
[2026-03-15 02:12:45] sweeper: freed 0 pages (fragmentation prevents coalescing)
```
Jia T.: that pattern matches a fragmentation-driven slow-bleed: pages can't coalesce so sweeper can't reclaim. We should make eviction more aggressive and increase sweeper frequency temporarily.
Omar V.: agree. Plan: 1) bump kv eviction watermark to 0.6 2) lower kv page compaction threshold 3) restart sweeper on affected nodes in a rolling fashion. I'll coordinate the restarts to avoid mass bounces.
Maria C.: preparing commands — patching runtime config on cluster rvw-prod -> will route new config to the control plane (quick patch):
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"kv_eviction_watermark":"0.6","kv_compact_threshold":"0.3"}}'
# then rollout restart of sweeper DaemonSet on affected nodes
kubectl -n inference rollout restart daemonset/kv-sweeper --selector=node=rvw-prod-gpu-05
```
deploy-bot: Canary fallback triggered for model-group llama-13b: variant -> llama-13b-quantized-evict (auto-fallback). Canary started on rvw-prod-gpu-12.
Linda P.: Support question — are customers seeing errors? We have a cluster of 5 tenants that reported 502s starting ~02:10 UTC. Any ETA to mitigation?
Maria C.: we're in progress. Initial changes applied to control plane and a single-sweep restart done on rvw-prod-gpu-05. Early telemetry: OOM error rate dropped from 12/min to 4/min on that node. Still elevated but improving.
Alex R.: also please push a runtime flag to disable attention paging for the heavy tails on that model class, fallback to standard attention for new sessions until we stabilize. That avoids fragmented kv growth for new requests. Command (on control plane API):
```json
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/config
{ "model_selector": "llama-13b*", "attention_paging_enabled": false }
```
Maria C.: applied attention paging off for llama-13b* at 02:34 UTC. New sessions are landing on fallback variant.
Maria C.: sweeper log after restart:
```
[2026-03-15 02:38:12] sweeper: aggressive-mode enabled (watermark=0.6)
[2026-03-15 02:38:14] sweeper: freed 12.1GB in 2m across 3 nodes (coalesced 14k pages)
[2026-03-15 02:38:14] sweeper: fragmentation metric dropped 75% -> 42%
```
incident-bot: NOTE: OOM rate decreased cluster-wide by 65% in last 15m, but fragmentation remains above healthy threshold. Recommend heap/kv profile and snapshot for postmortem.
Jia T.: please capture heap profiles and a near-real-time allocation histogram from the runtime on the affected nodes. Also schedule an eng-runtime debug window to reproduce fragmentation locally. I'll open an incident ticket and set severity to SEV2 due to customer errors.
Omar V.: I'll roll restarts to rvw-prod-gpu-12 and rvw-prod-gpu-07 in 10m windows, monitoring tail latency. We'll avoid more than one node offline at once.
Maria C.: quick mitigation note for handoff: - root cause hypothesis: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + suboptimal eviction cadence (sweeper too timid) -> slow resident growth -> OOM. - mitigations applied: eviction watermark 0.6, kv_compact_threshold 0.3, attention paging disabled for llama-13b*, canary fallback to quantized-evict variant, rolling sweeper restarts. - immediate impact: OOM rates down 65%, 5 tenants saw 502s intermittently (now reduced). - outstanding: capture profiles, permanent fix: improve coalescing logic & more robust page compaction.
Linda P.: I'll draft a short customer-facing note and coordinate with growth for any escalation.
Alex R.: eng-runtime: please triage compaction algorithm and sweeper heuristics; if needed push a hotfix that forces immediate compaction passes when fragmentation delta > 20% over 6h.
Maria C.: handing off to the next on-call (Omar V.) — moving into monitoring + postmortem prep. Key artifacts: grafana link (oom-spike), k8s pod logs (rvw-prod-gpu-05 & -12), sweeper logs, runtime-config diff. Handoff ts: 1777777890.
Omar V.: ack, picking up. Will keep the mitigations active until eng-runtime confirms a safe rollout of a fix. I'll post updates in #incidents if anything changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Transition to monitoring phase. SEV2 -> mitigated for now. Next steps: collect profiles, schedule eng-runtime debug, plan postmortem in 48h. :white_check_mark:
